newsitem.title: USA: CME March lumber ends limit down, cash still weak.
newsitem.headline: CME March lumber ends limit down, cash still weak.

text.p: March CME lumber futures ended down the daily limit of $10.00 per thousand board feet, knocked lower by a weak tone to cash lumber, traders said.
March closed limit down at $401.40 per tbf and May finished $8.00 lower at $375.30. Other months ended $7.10 to $3.10 per tbf lower.

Canadian mills still need to boost exports to meet their allocations before the end of the quarter and export year under the export agreeement which ends March 31. In the meantime, cash trade is slow with wholesalers undercutting mill asking levels to move wood, traders said.
"They (wholesalers) are not selling for much more than they paid for the (lumber)," said Curt Cunningham, President of Pacific Futures Trading.

Spreading of long May/short March added to the weakness in March which finished with more than 200 cars left to be sold at the limit down. Options also point to further weakness with the March synthetic trading down $5 at $396.40, they said.
Cargill Investor Services was an early buyer while Refco and stops pushed prices down. Selling also developed as the market was overbought after Friday's corrective rally, they added.
